pr_title: Implement resetting of created streams for annotations
pr_body:
Fixes #12337.

Note that I tried to use a non-caching getter here, but I did not manage to get that to work. I found that if it were to work it would require more code changes and I found it not that great that we would not cache the appearance stream on the instance because it would lead to recalculation every time the annotation goes out of view. Therefore, after checking the alternatives, this solution seemed the simplest.
pr_comments: Would it be possible to add a `fbf`-test for this, since unless I'm completely misunderstanding how those work they should currently trigger the bug!?

issue_context.title: Highlight disappears when page is re-rendered after being out of view
issue_context.body:
Steps to reproduce:

1. Go to https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/web/viewer.html.
2. Download https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=0B6YhVF9p-y2AU0RlYjRKakFQRjQ and open it with the viewer.
3. Notice that the highlight (without appearance stream) is rendered correctly on the first page.
4. Scroll to the last page.
5. Scroll to the first page.
6. Notice that the highlight is gone.

I don't directly have an idea how this can happen. As far as I know, the complete page is re-rendered after being out of view, so we _should_ also re-render the annotations, but apparently we don't. This is not intermittent and reproduces 100% of the time.

/cc @calixteman Perhaps you have any ideas why the second time the appearance stream is not generated/rendered?
comments:
It looks like we parse the annotations only once and store them in `this._parsedAnnotations`, but even then the `this.appearance` on the annotation should be set. We loop over the parsed annotations and include their operator lists here:

https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/60ffac04808da1e427b395f783c028d84d5b8ecb/src/core/document.js#L334-L353

Adding a `appearance.dict.get("Resources").get("XObject").get("Fm0").reset();` at https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/master/src/core/annotation.js#L558 fixes the issue... 
I had this idea because of the `reset` just before.
I can add a bool and a check to add this `reset` but I've the impress we can do better. Any suggestions ?

I wonder why that fixes the problem though. I can only imagine the current `reset` usage is to reduce memory usage because the operator list is rendered, so we can discard the appearance stream. However, when re-rendering I would expect it to just be recalculated. Why is that not the case now and is the case when you reset that particular element?

Ah, `reset` on a `StringStream` doesn't do what I thought it did. It doesn't clear the stream, but it puts the reading position back to the beginning of the stream. In that case it makes sense that we need to reset this new string stream too because once we read it, we're at the end and a new invocation will simply do nothing because we already read everything...

I think your solution will indeed work, but indeed there should be a better solution. I have some ideas now, but I'll give this some more thought and make a patch in the coming days. Thank you for providing the right direction here!

> It doesn't clear the stream,

Note that it's *not* suppose to either...

> but it puts the reading position back to the beginning of the stream.

... and this is the one and only purpose of the `reset` method, which exist on all of the various Stream-implementations.

> I think your solution will indeed work, but indeed there should be a better solution.

The problem with the idea in https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/issues/12337#issuecomment-687900775 is that it feels very hacky, and in general it's also not a workable solution.

---

The first thing you want to (and should) do here is understand *exactly* why things break, and in particular what's special about the newly added code. As you might remember, we don't cache Streams on the `XRef`-instance partly because of size considerations *and* partly because of the problems associated with resetting their start-position.

In this case though, the issue with the Streams in the `_setDefaultAppearance` method is that they're not referred to by `Ref`s (since you cannot just create `Ref`s, if they're not already in the PDF document) but instead created/referenced explicitly. Given that the result of `_setDefaultAppearance` is cached in `this.appearance`, you end you keeping some Streams alive in an (for other parts of the code-base) completely unexpected fashion.

My somewhat naive idea, given that `_setDefaultAppearance` is only relevant to a subset of documents without complete data, would be if it's possible to e.g. cache the `buffer` and some related state and instead lazily create `this.appearance` using a non-caching getter in this case!?

review_comments: I think that's a valid concern and we might be able to improve this by unconditionally including `this.appearance` so we don't need to do it at the various call sites.

I pushed a new version that centralizes the `this.appearance` pushing in the `Annotation` constructor as much as possible instead of in various places. Would you still like to have this `PDFJSDev` addition or does the current solution suffice?

> I pushed a new version that centralizes the `this.appearance` pushing in the `Annotation` constructor as much as possible instead of in various places.

While this obviously *reduces* the risk of future issues, as far as I can tell it doesn't completely eliminate it.

> Would you still like to have this `PDFJSDev` addition or does the current solution suffice?

Yes, please add those checks as well here!
They'll *only* apply in non-PRODUCTION or TESTING builds, i.e. won't affect the run-time in releases, and seem like an easy way to prevent future bugs.
Done in the new commit, including the FBF test which failed on master but passes with this patch applied.
